rationale:
The example's scenario is a requirement with an `{impl}` citation in one function, a `{test}` citation in another, and a terminology reference. The expected outcome is that the initial prompt contains the complete requirement, both functions and the definition. The tests cover this.

- **End-to-end test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs` has `Fixture::new` and `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`, and both carry `{test}` references to the example.
  - `Fixture::new` builds `requirements.ready` with the text "SECRET_REQUIREMENT_TEXT MUST implement {term}`terms.readiness`." It adds a definition `terms.readiness`, whose text is `SECRET_DEFINITION_TEXT`.
  - `Fixture::new` also writes `src/lib.rs` with `{impl}` on `pub fn ready()` and `{test}` on `fn ready_test()`.
  - The CLI test inspects the first request's prompt. It asserts the prompt contains the requirement text, `SECRET_DEFINITION_TEXT`, `fn ready()` and `fn ready_test()`.
  - It also asserts that the old stored rationale is absent.
  - It then checks the recorded evidence inputs. These include `src/lib.rs` `fn[ready]` and the `terms.readiness` definition.
- **Bundle-level unit test.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs` has `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors`, which carries a `{test}` reference to the example.
  - It asserts that `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` and `fn[test_ready]` are contributed, and that the enclosing `impl[Thing]` is not.
  - It asserts that the terminology definitions are contributed (a count of 2).
  - It asserts that the subject's cited requirement (`requirements.base`) and the example (`requirements.case`) are included, and that the distant requirement and earlier evidence inputs are not.

The tests cover the scenario's setup and each expected outcome. They show the requirement text, the implementation function, the test function and the definition in the initial prompt and inputs.

:::{req} authoring_input
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.

An in-source `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference to the subject, except a `{fixme}` inside one of the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, contributes the source containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} initial_prompt
The initial request MUST provide the eight tool definitions above and the
following prompt. The harness MUST replace `{{subject_kind}}` with `requirement`
or `example`, `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name,
`{{habeas_background}}`, `{{reference_roles}}`, and `{{distributed_background}}`
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.habeas_background`, `{{judgment_rules}}` under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and `{{mandatory_inputs}}` with the
complete mandatory inputs as a JSON array using
the existing evidence-input formats. It MUST replace `{{subject_task}}`, for a requirement, with the text of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.requirement_task` followed by that of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.testing_bar` and, for a distributed requirement,
that of {cite}`requirements.authoring.distributed_task`; for an example, with the
text of {cite}`requirements.authoring.example_task`. The template MUST otherwise
be used as written. Their review guidance MUST follow
{impl}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, {cite}`requirements.examples.evidence`,
and {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
```text
# Task
Assess whether a project's source code and tests satisfy one {{subject_kind}}.
Your determination should be the one any careful reviewer would reach from the
same text and sources.
Subject: {{subject_kind}} {{subject_name}}
Judge against: the subject's text.
# Background: Habeas terms
{{habeas_background}}
{{reference_roles}}
# Your task
The mandatory inputs at the end contain the subject, the requirements and
examples it cites, the vocabulary definitions it uses, and every source item
carrying an {impl}, {test}, or {fixme} reference to it. Each {fixme} input shows
the state of the issues it names.
Cited requirements and examples are context: when the subject requires behavior
under or following a cited requirement, check that the subject's code applies
that requirement in the subject's case, but do not reassess the cited
requirement's own implementation or tests. For a requirement subject, the code
that decides to apply the cited requirement in the subject's case implements
that obligation of the subject, even when it only calls code implementing the
cited requirement; it needs its own {impl} reference and a test.
When another requirement's text carries an {impl} reference to the subject,
assess only whether that text carries out the obligations it covers; do not
reassess its implementation or tests, and those obligations need no test here.
{{subject_task}}
# How to judge
{{judgment_rules}}
# Submitting
Choose true when your task finds no gap, {"FIXME": ["..."]} when every gap is
acknowledged, and false otherwise. Call submit_judgment exactly once with
determination and rationale. That tool call is your final answer.
# Mandatory inputs
{{mandatory_inputs}}
